candidates.tagline: The $25K EV that ships without paint, a radio, or any illusions
candidates.story: Slate Auto's bare-bones electric pickup is starting Q4 2026 deliveries with no factory paint (just raw plastic panels), no infotainment, no speakers, and hand-crank windows — software updates require you to plug your phone into a USB port.
candidates.why_funny: In 2026, the cutting-edge EV asks you to hand-crank your windows and plug your phone in like it's 2004.
candidates.alt: A light blue vinyl-wrapped Slate electric pickup truck with its hood open on display near the Space Needle in Seattle, surrounded by curious onlookers

candidates.tagline: Epic fired 1,000 programmers, then said 'programming is hard' and shipped a buggy AI launcher
candidates.story: Seven months after laying off 1,000 employees, Epic Games released a 'vibe coded' (AI-written) game launcher on October 14, 2026, explaining that 'programming is hard' — users immediately found it riddled with login errors and update bugs.
candidates.why_funny: Epic told a thousand programmers they weren't needed, then discovered they were needed.
candidates.alt: Screenshot of the new Epic Games Store Preview 0.95.2 launcher showing a dark game library grid with game tiles including Alan Wake 2, Control, and Hades
